title: SGGly: a web server for whole-protein; structure-guided analysis of candidate N-linked glycosylation sites.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded train.csv (36 MB), val.csv (4.5 MB), test.csv (4.6 MB) from the SGGly Data page, no login. Columns: Entry (UniProt accession), Position, Residue, N-linked-gly-label, PubMed-label. Rows 2,137,515 / 267,710 / 267,487 (total 2,672,712); proteins 3,667 / 460 / 287 (total 4,414); positives 12,515 / 1,677 / 1,441 (total 15,633); PubMed-supported 2,365 / 381 / 295 (total 3,041). No nulls, no duplicate (Entry, Position) rows, no protein shared between splits, all positives are Asn, 99.7% of positives sit on N-X-[not P]-S/T sequons; 21,246 sequons in total.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That labels come from UniProt CARBOHYD features of reviewed human entries; that the split is low-redundancy by global pairwise alignment; how 'confident negatives' were defined for the strict regime; the reported MCC 0.888 and AUC 0.987 and N-GlyDE benchmark numbers. Structural descriptors (AlphaFold/DSSP) are not in the CSVs.

a1_downloadable.note: Three CSVs downloaded directly from the server's Data page, no login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Binary per-residue label columns N-linked-gly-label and PubMed-label are present (checked); no construction needed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full sequence is present residue by residue and can be reassembled per protein (checked); structures would need AlphaFold DB lookups by UniProt accession, which is one bulk fetch.

a5_enough_rows.note: 21,246 sequons (candidate sites) with 15,633 positives; strict PubMed-supported positives 3,041 (counted in files).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 45 MB CSV; ESM-2 embeddings only needed at ~21k sequon positions
a6_fits_laptop.note: Embedding 4,414 proteins with a small ESM-2 on CPU is a few hours; long proteins need chunking.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Residues 2,672,712, proteins 4,414, positives 15,633, PubMed-supported 3,041 and sequons 21,246 all match the paper exactly (checked).

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are UniProt curator annotations; 80% (12,592) are annotation-only, some inferred by sequence similarity, so partly prediction-derived. The PubMed-label subset (3,041) traces to experiments; unlabelled sequons are not confirmed negatives.

B1.why: Three CSVs with identical five columns; train/val/test pre-split by protein (checked).

B2.why: All three parsed first try with pandas, no nulls (checked).

B3.why: Two label tiers mixing experimental and annotation-only evidence; strict tier must be chosen deliberately (checked columns).

B5.why: Zero duplicate (Entry, Position) rows and zero protein overlap across splits (checked).

B6.why: Columns self-explanatory but no README; negative definition only in paper text.

C1.why: Mostly a beat-the-benchmark task; re-evaluation on strict labels could be informative either way.

C2.why: LMNglyPred, EMNGly, StackGlyEmbed, CoNglyPred, DeepNGlyPred all open on GitHub, all protein-language-model based.

C3.why: Only weak angle: honest re-benchmark of open models on SGGly's low-redundancy strict split.

C4.why: Glycoproteomics mass spectrometry is costly, but sequon rule plus existing predictors are free.

C5.why: Published MCC 0.888 strict regime, and N-GlyDE benchmark numbers for many tools.

D1.why: ESM-2, an open protein language model, matches per-residue sequence input.

D2.why: Per-residue embeddings at sequon positions cached once on CPU, logistic head.

D3.why: ESM-2 is MIT licensed; SGGly data licence page exists but terms not read.

E1.why: Authors' low-redundancy protein-level split provided; zero protein overlap verified in files.

E3.why: Sequon-only rule and per-sequon majority class trivially computable.

E4.why: No replicate measurements; annotation-only versus PubMed tiers only hint at label noise.

E5.why: Known effect: N-X-T sequons glycosylated more often than N-X-S; Pro at X+2 position lowers occupancy.

E6.why: Label shuffle and embedding-versus-motif ablation straightforward.

E7.why: N-GlyDE benchmark and N-GlycositeAtlas are independent sets used by prior papers.

E8.why: SGGly test split published, so their MCC can be checked against our model on same rows.

G2.why: AlphaFold DB structures and GlyGen/GlyConnect site evidence, joinable on UniProt accession.

G3.why: One protein per accession, one AlphaFold model per canonical sequence; isoform mismatches possible.

G4.why: Structure adds accessibility context, but CoNglyPred and SGGly already did that.

H1.why: Negatives are unannotated sequons, not experimentally confirmed unoccupied sites.

H2.why: Human reviewed UniProt only, one curation source.

H4.why: Paper explicitly states 80% of positives are annotation-only.

I1.why: Glycobiology and glycoproteomics labs generally; no named group would switch tools.

I2.why: Marginal: many open predictors already prioritise sequons.

I3.why: Per-sequon ranking roughly matches choosing sites to mutate or validate.

I4.why: Sequon rule captures 99.7% of positives; ML only separates occupied from unoccupied sequons (~74% positive).

J1.why: Real modelling with embeddings, grouped splits, external benchmark.

J2.why: Sequon biology is textbook, but label noise makes errors hard to judge.

J3.why: A re-benchmark table of open tools is a small shareable result.

J4.why: Could be a two-weekend project; not yet written down.

integration.partner_dataset: AlphaFold DB structures plus GlyGen / N-GlycositeAtlas mass-spectrometry site evidence
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequons unannotated in UniProt but occupied in mass-spectrometry atlases share structural features that annotation-trained models miss?

controls.positive_control: Model must rank N-X-T above N-X-S sequons and recover the sequon rule from embeddings alone.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within protein; replace embeddings with random vectors; both should fall to sequon-only baseline.

honest_claim_h3: Ranks which N-X-S/T sequons in reviewed human proteins UniProt curators annotate as N-glycosylated, where 80% of positives are annotation-only and unannotated sequons are treated as negatives without experimental proof.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's sequence around each candidate sugar-attachment motif to predict whether that asparagine actually carries an N-linked sugar.
plain_idea.train_on: Each of 21,246 candidate motifs (asparagine-X-serine/threonine) in 4,414 human proteins, described by a protein language model's per-residue summary of the sequence.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the site is annotated as N-glycosylated in UniProt; 3,041 of 15,633 positives are backed by published experiments, the rest by curator annotation.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Glycobiologists choosing which sites to mutate or check by mass spectrometry could prioritise; but many open tools already do this, so the gain is likely marginal.

label_elsewhere.sources: UniProt CARBOHYD features for other species (known resource), GlyGen and GlyConnect site databases, N-GlycositeAtlas mass-spectrometry sites (named in search results as benchmark).
label_elsewhere.why: Mass-spectrometry atlases give an independent, experiment-based test set to check whether annotation-trained models find real sites.

pitch.headline: A clean, pre-split per-residue table: 2,672,712 residues, 4,414 human proteins, 15,633 glycosylation sites, every count matching the paper exactly.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: It flags which 3,041 positives have published experimental support versus 12,592 annotation-only, and splits by protein with zero overlap (verified), allowing honest strict-label evaluation.
pitch.the_win: Show whether open tools like LMNglyPred (MCC 0.717 on N-GlyDE) keep their score on SGGly's strict PubMed-supported test split of 295 positives.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A table of how far published glycosylation predictors drop on low-redundancy, experiment-backed labels; little biology learned beyond that.
pitch.who_wants_it: Groups building glycosylation predictors (Ascher lab, KC lab at Michigan Tech) deciding which benchmark to report.

ml_idea: Frozen ESM-2 per-residue embeddings at each sequon plus motif one-hot, logistic or gradient-boosted head; train on annotation labels, evaluate on PubMed-supported subset and N-GlyDE; compare against open LMNglyPred.

effort.compute_note: Estimated: 4,414 proteins of mean ~600 residues through ESM-2 35M/150M on CPU at ~0.5-2 s each; head on 21k rows is seconds. Nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute sequon-only plus N-X-T/S motif baseline MCC on the strict test split; if near 0.888 there is nothing left to learn.

verdict_reason: Data is clean and verified, but the task is crowded with open protein-language-model predictors, labels are mostly curator annotation, and the sequon rule alone captures 99.7% of positives; little angle remains.
